0. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian
Standard ( Part I ) was adopted by the Indian Institution on 23 June 1977, after the draft finalized by the Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electronics communication Division Council. Standards Capacitors and Tele-

0.2 This standard applies to polar and bi-polar fixed solid electrolyte tantalum capacitors of hermetically sealed, moulded and dipped types. It covers capacitors for long life applications and for general purpose applications. Capacitors for special purpose applications may need additional requirements. 0.2.1 Dimensional tantalum capacitors standard. and specific requirements will be covered in the of various subsequent types of fixed parts of this

0.3 The general requirements and tests for all types of fixed capacitors are covered in IS : 7305 ( Part I )-1973*, which is a necessary adjunct to this standard. 0.4 In the preparation the following: 40 of this standard, assistance has been derived from

( Sectt) 325 Fixed tentalum capacitors with liquid electrolyte. Selection of methods of test and general ments; International Electrotechnical Commission.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard ( Part I ) covers the general requirements and methods of tests for judging the electrical, mechanical, and climatic properties of solid electrolyte tantalum capacitors intended for use in electronic and other similar equipment. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.0 For the purpose of this standard, the terms and definitions IS : 7305 (Part I )-19731_ and those given below shall apply. given in

2.1 Long Life Grade Capacitors - Capacitors intended for applications where a high degree of stability of characteristics over a long life is essential.
NOTE 1 -The materials are so chosen and manufacture PO carried improved performance is obtained with consequent increase in life. test. NOTE 2 -The long life will correspond to 2 000 hours duration out, that

for endurance

2.2 General Purpose Grade Capacitor-A capacitor intended for applications where the high performance level of long life grade capacitors is not required.
NOTE-The life will correspond to 1 000 hours duration for endurance test.

2.3 Capacitance of an Electrolytic Capacitor - The capacitance of an equivalent circuit having capacitance and resistance in series, measured with alternating current of approximately sinusoidal waveform at the specified frequency. 2.4 Reverse Voltage applied to the capacitor 3. CLIMATIC ( for Polar Capacitors Only) -A terminal in the reverse polarity direction. voltage

3.1 The solid tantalum into climatic categories 1961:.

3.2 Capacitors covered in this standard shall belong to one of the three categories given in Table 1 based on their ability to withstand the climatic severities.

The IS1 Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by IS1 and operated by the producer. 8.1.1.2 Number of samples - Unless otherwise specified, of samples for each type shall be 25 or 33, with 3 spares.

8.1.1.3 Selection of samples-The samples shall be representative of the range of values of the type under consideration. Samples shall comprise quantities as equal as possible of the largest and the smallest case size specimen with the lowest and the highest rated voltages. When there are more than four case sizes, an intermediate case size shall also be chosen for testing. For each case size, the samples with the highest capacitance Samples of maximum capacitance at its highest voltage shall be chosen. as well as those with maximum voltage at its highest capacitance shall be chosen.

Tests test shall I )-1973* be carried out in accordance with the following additional

8.3.1 Leakage Current -This with 7.3.4 of IS : 7305 (Part details/modifications:

a) Measuring Conditions -The total circuit resistance shall be between 1000 and 10 000 ohms and the leakage current shall be measured after charging the capacitor through the specified resistor for five minutes. In case of bi-polar capacitors the measurements shall first be made in one direction after an electrification period of five minutes. The polarity shall then be reversed and the measurements made again after a further electrification period not exceeding five minutes. b) Requirements - The leakage current at 27 5 values specified in the relevant specification.

8.3.4 Voltage Proof of the Insulation ( .h'ot A$#icable for Category 3 ) This test shall be carried out in accordance with 7.3.1 of IS : 7305 ( Part I )1973* with the following additional details/modifications: a) Measuring Conditions-A metal foil shall be wrapped closely around the full length of the body of the capacitor, protruding by at least 5 mm from each end, provided a minimum space of 1 mm is maintained between the metal foil and the point of emergence of the terminations. The ends of the foil shall not be folded over the ends of the capacitor. When it is not possible to maintain a minimum spacing of 1 mm the protrusion of the foil shall be reduced as may be necessary to establish the 1 mm space. When applicable, the V block method is permitted as an alternative except for the specimens where the distance between the point of emergence of terminations and the plate would be less than 1 mm. A direct voltage, as given below, shall be applied between the metal foil and the termination connected to the body of the capacitor: Category requirements

8.5.1.2 Dry heat-This test shall be carried out in accordance with 7.5.1.2 of IS : 7305 ( Part I )-1973* with no rated voltage applied. Duration of the test shall be 16 hours unless otherwise specified in the relevant specification. After recovery the shall be no visible damage Marking shall be legible, capacitors shall be visually examined. There and shall show no seepage of sealing material.

8.5.1.3 Damp heat ( accelerated) jirst cycle - This test shall be carried out in accordance with 7.5.1.3 of IS : 7305 ( Part I)-1973* with no rated voltage applied. After recovery the capacitors shall be visually examined. There shall be no visible damage and shall show no seepage of sealing material. Marking shall be legible. 8.5.1.4 Cold-This test shall be carried out in accordance with 7.5.1.4 of IS : 7305 (Part I )-1973" with no rated voltage applied. The duration of exposure shall be 2 hours unless otherwise specified in the relevant specification. During the last 10 minutes.of shall be applied to the specimens. the period of exposure the rated voltage

8.5.1.5 Low air pressure - This test shall be carried out in accordance with 7.5.1.5 of IS : 7305 (Part I )-1973" with the following additional details/modifications. No initial measurements are required. Conditioning of capacitors shall consist of subjecting to an air pressure of 20 mbar for a period of 5 minutes the ambient temperature being between 15�C and 35�C. During the last minute of the conditioning the rated direct voltage shall be applied. APPENDIX A ( Clauses 8.4.3.2 and 8.4.3.3)
SPECIAL BENDING A-l. OBJECT TEST

A-l.1 The object of this test is to determine the ability of the termination to withstand the bending likely to be applied during normal assembly operation. A-2. APPARATUS A-2.1 The apparatus for special bending test is given in Fig. 1.

See Note

=! 6.35

APPROX

NOTE -The diameter of the countersunk the diameter of the lead wire.

All dimensions in millimetres.

FIG. 1 APPARATUS FOR SPECIAL BENDING Tess 20

16 : 8507 (Part I) - 1977

A-3. PROCEDURE
A-3.1 The lead shall be inserted into the hole of the fixture ( Fig. 1 ) so that the lower side of the weld on the soldered joint is approximately flush with the surface of the fixture. The case shall be forced over in such a manner that the tantalum stub is maintained in its axial position as closely as possible while bending the lead until the end of the case touches the top surface of the fixture.
A-3.1.1 When the case is returned to its normal position, one bend will have been completed. A-3.1.2 A-3.1.3 Succeeding bends shall be made in the alternate directions. The lead shall meet four bends.
